A folded section can clarify the upper articulation without losing the compact neighborhood-building character.
Align the section logic across the site-access relationship so the void and threshold remain legible from the road edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen section readability by replacing the generic void emphasis with a more intentional profiled hall-like section family while preserving the same dominant mass and parcel fit.
Slightly tighten the carved void so the street-facing threshold reads as a clearer public cut rather than a broad subtraction.
Keep the void aligned to the verified access side in the program frame so the public threshold remains coherent.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent primary mass with a legible carved internal slot and a stable anchored base. It is not over-fragmented and it does respond to the parcel rather than simply filling a box. The blue frontage edge is answered by a visible ground-side void/entry seam in plan and by the carved open condition in the mass, which is appropriate for neighborhood living. However, the section/silhouette is still somewhat arbitrary: the top slot and stepped/roof articulation do not yet create a strongly resolved programmatic section, so the form remains only moderately convincing as a mixed-use neighborhood building. The main risk is that the silhouette can be read as a generic extruded block with a subtraction rather than a fully integrated public ground and upper hierarchy. Overall it passes program fit because the mass plausibly supports a compact street building with active threshold and usable void, but it would benefit from a more intentional section response and stronger void-to-mass continuity.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked platform massing with a carved upper void reads as a coherent mixed-use datum and supports a clear public-ground relation.
